title: Bypassed Core Formation in Milky Way-Mass SIDM Halos: Implications for the Local Group Past-Pericenter Scenario
comment: 21 pages, 13 figures, comments are welcome
summary: We consider a scenario in which the Milky Way (MW) and M31 have had a previous pericentric passage, and investigate its compatibility with self-interacting dark matter (SIDM). Using initial conditions sampled from Local Group (LG) analogues in the IllustrisTNG simulation, we perform controlled re-simulations of the MW-M31 orbit, evolving the system under both standard cold dark matter (CDM) and various SIDM cross-sections. We find that the deep baryonic potential of the MW preconditions the halo's thermal structure, establishing an initial negative temperature gradient. This drives SIDM halos to bypass the standard core-formation phase and enter immediate core-collapse, resulting in monotonically increasing central densities. In full orbital simulations, the compact stellar component (disk/bulge) of the MW analog remains robust against tidal disruption for pericenter distances as close as $r_{\rm peri}\lesssim20$ kpc during an encounter at cosmic time $\sim8$ Gyr. The diffuse stellar halo is comparatively more susceptible, facing disruption for $r_{\rm peri}\lesssim100$ kpc. Our results demonstrate a dichotomy in structural evolution: the compact disk/bulge is sensitive to intrinsic SIDM thermodynamics but dynamically robust against the pericenter encounter, whereas the diffuse stellar halo is largely independent of the specific SIDM model but more vulnerable to orbital tidal disruptions.

AI.tldr: SIDM halos with preconditioned thermal structure bypass core formation and enter immediate core-collapse during MW-M31 encounters, creating a dichotomy where compact stellar components are thermodynamically sensitive but dynamically robust, while diffuse halos are SIDM-independent but tidally vulnerable.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether a previous pericentric passage between the Milky Way and M31 is compatible with self-interacting dark matter models, and to understand how SIDM thermodynamics interacts with orbital dynamics in Local Group encounters.
AI.method: Used initial conditions from Local Group analogues in IllustrisTNG simulation, performed controlled re-simulations of MW-M31 orbit under both CDM and various SIDM cross-sections, analyzed thermal structure preconditioning by baryonic potential, and examined tidal disruption thresholds for different stellar components.
AI.result: Deep baryonic potential establishes negative temperature gradient that drives SIDM halos into immediate core-collapse with monotonically increasing central densities. Compact stellar components (disk/bulge) remain robust against tidal disruption for pericenter distances <20 kpc, while diffuse stellar halos disrupt for <100 kpc. Structural evolution shows dichotomy: compact components sensitive to SIDM thermodynamics but dynamically robust, diffuse halos SIDM-independent but tidally vulnerable.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates that MW-M31 pericentric encounters are compatible with SIDM models, revealing a fundamental dichotomy in structural evolution where different stellar components respond differently to SIDM thermodynamics versus orbital dynamics, with implications for constraining SIDM cross-sections from Local Group observations.

title: Temperature asymmetry in the Milky Way's hot circumgalactic medium induced by the Magellanic Clouds
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS, 6 pages, 3 figures
summary: The Milky Way is surrounded by a hot diffuse circumgalactic medium (CGM) with temperatures of millions of degrees. Recent X-ray observations with the eROSITA satellite discovered a significant temperature asymmetry of this hot CGM, with the southern hemisphere being on average hotter than the northern one by a relative difference of $Δ T/T \approx 12\%$, where $T$ is averaged over the entire CGM. In this Letter, we investigate whether the passage of the Magellanic Clouds can be responsible for this asymmetry by means of a hydrodynamical/N-body simulation. In the simulation, the Magellanic Clouds induce a relative motion of the Milky Way's disc of up to 40 km/s. This motion leads to compression of the CGM gas in the southern hemisphere, resulting in an overall temperature increase in that region. We estimate a south-north temperature difference of $Δ T/T \approx 13-20\%$, consistent with the observations. We find that this temperature asymmetry is a recent phenomenon that began ~100 Myr ago.

AI.tldr: The Magellanic Clouds' passage induces Milky Way disc motion, compressing the southern CGM and creating a 13-20% temperature asymmetry consistent with eROSITA observations.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed temperature asymmetry in the Milky Way's hot circumgalactic medium (CGM), where the southern hemisphere is ~12% hotter than the northern one, as detected by eROSITA X-ray observations.
AI.method: Hydrodynamical/N-body simulation investigating whether the passage of the Magellanic Clouds can create the observed temperature asymmetry by inducing relative motion of the Milky Way's disc.
AI.result: The simulation shows Magellanic Clouds induce up to 40 km/s disc motion, compressing southern CGM gas and creating 13-20% temperature difference, consistent with observations. The asymmetry began ~100 Myr ago.
AI.conclusion: The Magellanic Clouds' passage can explain the observed CGM temperature asymmetry through induced disc motion and southern hemisphere compression, making this a recent (~100 Myr) phenomenon.

title: The Hubble sequence in JWST CEERS from unbiased galaxy morphologies
comment: 18 pages, 4 appendices; submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary:
Whether the "Hubble sequence" of galaxy morphologies exists up to z~4 is still disputed, and one of the challenges is characterizing galaxy structure consistently across a wide range of redshifts. To enable a fair comparison across cosmic time, we constructed "absolute" images of galaxies spanning 0.15<z<4.5 and 8<log $M_{\star}$<11 from HST CANDELS and JWST CEERS surveys, by matching the effective resolution and surface brightness limit of galaxies, accounting for cosmological dimming and evolution in size and mass-to-light ratio. We measured the structural parameters of 2825 galaxies and used the UMAP technique to study the evolution of the morphological phase space.
  We find a continuous sequence spanning late-type to early-type galaxies, with no redshift gradient - indicating that a Hubble-like sequence is established by z~4. We show that our approach recovers a cleaner separation between early- and late-type galaxies than visual classifications. By tracing progenitors using empirical mass assembly histories, we find that progenitors of low-mass galaxies are predominantly star-forming disks at all epochs. Progenitors of massive galaxies follow two distinct paths: a stable star-forming disk population with little structural evolution, and an early-type population that builds up rapidly from irregular progenitors and quenches within a few Gyr, consistent with a compaction-driven quenching scenario.

AI.tldr: The study finds that a Hubble-like galaxy morphology sequence exists up to z~4 by using consistent structural measurements across cosmic time, revealing distinct evolutionary paths for low-mass and massive galaxies.
AI.motivation: To resolve the dispute about whether the Hubble sequence of galaxy morphologies exists at high redshifts (up to z~4) by enabling fair structural comparisons across cosmic time through consistent image processing and measurement techniques.
AI.method: Constructed "absolute" images of 2825 galaxies (0.15<z<4.5) from HST CANDELS and JWST CEERS surveys by matching effective resolution and surface brightness limits, accounting for cosmological dimming and evolution in size and mass-to-light ratio. Measured structural parameters and used UMAP technique to study morphological phase space evolution. Traced progenitors using empirical mass assembly histories.
AI.result: Found a continuous morphological sequence spanning late-type to early-type galaxies with no redshift gradient, indicating Hubble-like sequence established by z~4. Approach recovers cleaner separation between early- and late-type galaxies than visual classifications. Low-mass galaxy progenitors are predominantly star-forming disks at all epochs. Massive galaxy progenitors follow two paths: stable star-forming disks with little structural evolution, and early-type population that builds rapidly from irregular progenitors and quenches within few Gyr, consistent with compaction-driven quenching.
AI.conclusion: Hubble sequence exists up to z~4 when using consistent structural measurements. Galaxy evolution follows mass-dependent paths: low-mass galaxies maintain disk-dominated structure, while massive galaxies exhibit bifurcated evolution with compaction-driven quenching playing key role in early-type formation.

title: Primordial Neutron Stars
comment: 6 pages + appendices, 3 figures
summary: We propose a novel cosmological scenario in which baryonic neutron stars could plausibly form in the early universe. If baryogenesis initially produces an excessively-large baryon asymmetry, $Y_B \gg 10^{-10},$ the baryonic mass inside the horizon can exceed the minimum neutron star mass before big bang nucleosynthesis (BBN). While this large asymmetry is present, non-relativistic baryons can dominate the universe and enhanced density perturbations on small scales can gravitationally collapse Hubble patches shortly after horizon re-entry. For some initial perturbations, just below the threshold for black hole formation, this collapse will be arrested only by nuclear pressure, possibly resulting in neutron star formation. Afterwards, there must be a large entropy injection to restore the observed baryon asymmetry, $Y_B \sim 10^{-10}$, and preserve the successful predictions of standard BBN. Unlike neutron stars that form from stellar collapse, primordial neutron stars can, in principle, be as light as $\sim 0.1 M_\odot$, limited only by the nuclear equation of state.

AI.tldr: Primordial neutron stars could form in early universe from gravitational collapse of baryon-dominated regions if initial baryon asymmetry was much larger than observed, with subsequent entropy injection restoring standard BBN conditions.
AI.motivation: To explore novel cosmological scenarios where neutron stars could form primordially, potentially explaining light neutron stars that cannot form through standard stellar evolution pathways.
AI.method: Propose scenario where initial baryon asymmetry Y_B >> 10^{-10} allows baryons to dominate universe early, enabling gravitational collapse of enhanced density perturbations into neutron stars via nuclear pressure support rather than black hole formation.
AI.result: Primordial neutron stars could form with masses as low as ~0.1 M⊙, limited only by nuclear equation of state, unlike stellar-collapse neutron stars which have higher minimum masses.
AI.conclusion: Early universe baryon-dominated phase with large initial asymmetry could produce primordial neutron stars, requiring subsequent entropy injection to restore observed baryon asymmetry while preserving standard BBN predictions.

title: Colloquium: Radio astronomy with the Arecibo 305-m telescope: In contemporaneous context
comment: 26 pages, 20 figures. doi.org/10.1103/mg21-4kcj
summary: Most scientific research begins in the context of the then-contemporary state of knowledge of the field and moves toward a deeper understanding of the subject. This colloquium presents the Arecibo telescope$^{'}$s contribution to radio astronomy from the point of view of its contemporary impact and relevance and how that evolved over the 57 years of its long life. Sometimes, serendipitous discoveries at Arecibo and elsewhere brought revolutionary changes to the field. Further, significant upgrades to the reflector, optics, receiving, and data-taking systems helped clear a pathway for a leap ahead. Charting these movements through time and without any claim to completeness, this Colloquium presents a progression through Arecibo telescope$^{'}$s role in the history of radio astronomy.

AI.tldr: Historical overview of Arecibo Observatory's 57-year contributions to radio astronomy, highlighting its evolving impact, serendipitous discoveries, and technological upgrades that advanced the field.
AI.motivation: To document and analyze the Arecibo telescope's historical significance in radio astronomy from its contemporary context, showing how its contributions evolved over time through both planned research and unexpected discoveries.
AI.method: Historical analysis through chronological progression, examining the telescope's impact within contemporary scientific contexts, serendipitous discoveries, and technological upgrades to its reflector, optics, receiving, and data-taking systems.
AI.result: The paper presents a comprehensive historical progression of Arecibo's role in radio astronomy, demonstrating how its contributions evolved through technological advancements and unexpected discoveries over 57 years.
AI.conclusion: Arecibo Observatory played a transformative role in radio astronomy history through sustained technological innovation, serendipitous discoveries, and evolving scientific impact that adapted to contemporary knowledge contexts over its operational lifetime.

title: FolpsD: combining EFT and phenomenological approaches for joint power spectrum and bispectrum analyses
comment: 42 pages, 19 figures. Supporting paper for the DESI DR2 full-shape key papers
summary: We present a theoretical model for the power spectrum and bispectrum of galaxy clustering that exploits the complementarity between small-scale power spectrum information and large-scale bispectrum measurements. We extend the FOLPS code by combining its one-loop EFT galaxy power spectrum with a tree-level galaxy bispectrum projected onto the tripolar spherical harmonics (Sugiyama) basis. To access additional small-scale information, we also consider a line-of-sight damping factor in both statistics, mirroring approaches commonly used in studies of redshift-space distortions. We test the model using DESI DR2 galaxy mocks. Even without damping, the joint analysis of the EFT power spectrum and bispectrum significantly improves constraints and reduces parameter degeneracies relative to power spectrum analyses alone. For LRG-like samples, including the damping further extends the range beyond $k\sim 0.3 \,h \text{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the power spectrum and $k \sim 0.24 \,h \text{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the bispectrum without introducing statistically significant parameter biases. This leads to up to $\sim 30\%$ tighter constraints on $A_s$ and $ω_{cdm}$. For low signal-to-noise tracers such as QSOs, however, the damping parameters are weakly constrained and can absorb noise fluctuations, leading to shifts in inferred parameters. Similar limitations may arise in models where cosmological information is encoded in power-spectrum shape features degenerate with the damping, such as scenarios with massive neutrinos. In contrast, for $w_0w_a$CDM we obtain $15\%$ and $21\%$ tighter constraints on $w_0$ and $w_a$, respectively, yielding a deviation from constant dark energy at slightly more than the $1σ$ level using full-shape information alone. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/cosmodesi/FolpsD

AI.tldr: The paper presents an enhanced theoretical model combining EFT galaxy power spectrum and bispectrum with line-of-sight damping, tested on DESI DR2 mocks, showing improved cosmological constraints.
AI.motivation: To exploit complementarity between small-scale power spectrum and large-scale bispectrum measurements for improved cosmological constraints, addressing limitations in current galaxy clustering analyses.
AI.method: Extends FOLPS code by combining one-loop EFT galaxy power spectrum with tree-level galaxy bispectrum projected onto tripolar spherical harmonics basis, adding line-of-sight damping factor to access small-scale information.
AI.result: Joint analysis significantly improves constraints and reduces parameter degeneracies. For LRG-like samples, damping extends range to k~0.3 h/Mpc (power spectrum) and k~0.24 h/Mpc (bispectrum) without biases, yielding ~30% tighter constraints on A_s and ω_cdm. For QSOs, damping parameters are weakly constrained and can cause parameter shifts.
AI.conclusion: The combined EFT power spectrum and bispectrum analysis with damping provides substantially improved cosmological constraints, particularly for w_0w_aCDM (15-21% tighter constraints on dark energy parameters), though caution needed for low signal-to-noise tracers where damping can absorb noise fluctuations.

title: What Heats the Dense Gas in the Galactic Center?
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ. 22 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables
summary: Previous studies using p-H$_2$CO $J=3$--$2$ transitions at 218 GHz suggested widespread high-temperature gas exceeding 60 K and even 100 K in the CMZ, with heating mechanisms possibly related to cosmic rays or turbulent dissipation. However, at temperatures above 100 K, p-H$_2$CO $J=3$--$2$ line emission may lead to significant overestimates of kinetic temperature. This study combines o-H$_2$CO $J=5$--$4$ data from JCMT with p-H$_2$CO $J=3$--$2$ data from APEX to analyze three molecular clouds (The Brick, Sgr A1, and Sgr A2) with high temperatures. We used the non-LTE radiative transfer code RADEX to model spectral lines and constrain physical parameters with multiple line ratios, obtaining more reliable kinetic temperatures. Our results show that the previously reported extreme temperatures ($>100$ K) based on p-H$_2$CO $J=3$--$2$ line ratios are revised downward, with the average kinetic temperatures now constrained to 84--95 K using o-H$_2$CO $J=5$--$4$ line ratios, indicating systematic overestimation in the earlier studies. Further analysis reveals that the relationship between temperature and gas line width aligns more closely with predictions from models incorporating both high cosmic ray ionization rate and turbulent heating, suggesting that these molecular clouds are likely heated by a combination of cosmic-ray and turbulent dissipation mechanisms.

AI.tldr: Previous studies using p-H₂CO J=3-2 transitions overestimated kinetic temperatures in CMZ molecular clouds; this study combines o-H₂CO J=5-4 and p-H₂CO J=3-2 data with RADEX modeling to obtain more reliable temperatures, revising extreme temperatures downward and suggesting combined cosmic-ray and turbulent heating mechanisms.
AI.motivation: Previous studies using p-H₂CO J=3-2 transitions at 218 GHz suggested widespread high-temperature gas exceeding 60-100 K in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ), but these measurements may lead to significant overestimates of kinetic temperature at temperatures above 100 K, necessitating more reliable temperature constraints.
AI.method: Combined o-H₂CO J=5-4 data from JCMT with p-H₂CO J=3-2 data from APEX to analyze three molecular clouds (The Brick, Sgr A1, and Sgr A2). Used non-LTE radiative transfer code RADEX to model spectral lines and constrain physical parameters with multiple line ratios for more reliable kinetic temperature determination.
AI.result: Previously reported extreme temperatures (>100 K) based on p-H₂CO J=3-2 line ratios are revised downward. Average kinetic temperatures are now constrained to 84-95 K using o-H₂CO J=5-4 line ratios, indicating systematic overestimation in earlier studies. Temperature-gas line width relationship aligns with models incorporating both high cosmic ray ionization rate and turbulent heating.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates that p-H₂CO J=3-2 line emission leads to significant temperature overestimates above 100 K. The revised temperatures (84-95 K) and their relationship with gas line widths suggest that CMZ molecular clouds are likely heated by a combination of cosmic-ray and turbulent dissipation mechanisms rather than single heating sources.

title: Bounding axion dark energy
comment: 17 pages + appendices + refs
summary: We study cosmological solutions of (pseudo)scalar theories with periodic potentials, in the presence of arbitrary cosmological fluids -- including a cosmological constant of either sign. Independently of the initial misalignment angle and field velocity, we derive an analytic bound that the axion mass parameter and decay constant fulfill as the universe decreases its acceleration rate, finding a natural application in models of thawing quintessence. As a first application, we illustrate the analytic handle our bound provides in bounding axion dark energy, after observational inputs from DESI and various supernovae data sets are taken into account. As a second application, we argue that our analytic bounds in combination with proposed quantum gravity constraints on axions exclude vast regions of parameter space. The combined constraints push the axion masses to be much larger than the Hubble scale, in tension with basic models of axion quintessence.

AI.tldr: Analytic bounds on axion mass and decay constant in cosmological models with periodic potentials, applied to thawing quintessence and constrained by observational data and quantum gravity considerations.
AI.motivation: To study cosmological solutions of (pseudo)scalar theories with periodic potentials in the presence of arbitrary cosmological fluids, including cosmological constants of either sign, and derive analytic bounds applicable to axion dark energy models.
AI.method: Derivation of analytic bounds on axion mass parameter and decay constant independent of initial conditions (misalignment angle and field velocity) as universe's acceleration rate decreases, applied to thawing quintessence models.
AI.result: Analytic bounds provide constraints on axion dark energy using DESI and supernovae data, and combined with quantum gravity constraints exclude large parameter regions, pushing axion masses above Hubble scale and challenging basic axion quintessence models.
AI.conclusion: The derived analytic bounds combined with observational data and quantum gravity constraints severely limit viable parameter space for axion quintessence, suggesting tension with basic models where axion masses are near Hubble scale.

title: Photoionization modelling of circumstellar nebulae using irregular grains
comment: 16 pages, 14 figures, 3 tables; accepted to MNRAS
summary: We study the effects of using the optical properties of irregular hexahedral grains in photoionization models of circumstellar nebulae around evolved stars. Dust opacities for the irregular grains were obtained from the scattering properties available in the TAMUdust2020 database and these were implemented in the spectral synthesis code cloudy. A sample of photoionization models that use opacities from both spherical and irregular hexahedral grains across a standard MRN size distribution (0.005 to 0.25 um) was produced. We consider the optical properties of graphite, amorphous carbon and silicate dust grains and find that differences between the model nebula continua calculated using spherical and irregular dust grains increase with the grain size, especially for graphite. In particular, we find that the luminosities at the infrared peak for the hexahedral grain models can be up to 60% higher than those from the equivalent spherical grain models for the largest grains. This result suggests that traditional spherical grain assumptions may lead to an overestimate of the dust mass in photoionized nebulae.

AI.tldr: Study shows irregular hexahedral dust grains produce up to 60% higher infrared luminosities than spherical grains in photoionization models, suggesting spherical assumptions may overestimate dust mass in circumstellar nebulae.
AI.motivation: To investigate how using realistic irregular hexahedral grain shapes (instead of traditional spherical approximations) affects photoionization modeling of circumstellar nebulae around evolved stars, particularly regarding dust opacity calculations and their impact on derived dust properties.
AI.method: Used optical properties of irregular hexahedral grains from TAMUdust2020 database, implemented in cloudy spectral synthesis code. Created photoionization models comparing spherical vs. irregular hexahedral grains across MRN size distribution (0.005-0.25 μm) for graphite, amorphous carbon, and silicate dust. Analyzed nebula continua differences.
AI.result: Differences between spherical and irregular grain models increase with grain size, especially for graphite. Hexahedral grain models show up to 60% higher luminosities at infrared peak compared to equivalent spherical grain models for largest grains.
AI.conclusion: Traditional spherical grain assumptions in photoionization modeling may lead to overestimation of dust mass in circumstellar nebulae. Realistic irregular grain shapes significantly affect infrared continuum predictions, particularly for larger grains.

title: The Cosmic Web and Its Filaments: Neutrino Mass from Topology and Persistent Homology
comment: 32 pages, 14 figures, 1 table. Submitted to ApJS (23 Feb 2026); under review
summary: We apply discrete Morse theory, global topology, and persistent homology to characterize the impact of massive neutrinos on the multiscale cosmic web, focusing on filaments. The topology of the cosmic web is sensitive to neutrino imprints, and persistence diagrams provide more information than commonly used summary statistics by quantifying the longevity of topological features across densities. This scale-adaptive, parameter-free formalism is powerful, as massive neutrinos affect halos, walls, filaments, and voids in distinct ways. Within this framework, we simultaneously assess their impact on tracers and skeleton structures and capture their multiscale signals across cosmic time. Discrete Morse theory is also well suited for particle-based neutrino implementations, often affected by Poisson shot noise, as it preserves the salient features of the underlying smooth field. Using two independent sets of N-body simulations, we present filament statistics and persistence diagrams in massive-neutrino cosmologies. Our results show that neutrinos leave distinct imprints on filaments and skeleton connectivity, producing mass-dependent signatures most pronounced at high redshift (z~2) and detectable at the few-percent level for masses as small as $M_ν\sim 0.1$ eV. Filaments thus provide an ideal environment for isolating neutrino effects. We also compare two implementations of massive neutrinos to assess systematics. Our study establishes a promising avenue for leveraging cosmic web topology, persistent homology, and environment-based statistics to constrain or directly detect neutrino mass and infer the mass hierarchy - a long-standing challenge in particle physics and a major objective of ongoing and upcoming galaxy redshift surveys (e.g., DES, DESI, Euclid, Rubin-LSST).

AI.tldr: Discrete Morse theory and persistent homology reveal neutrino mass imprints on cosmic filaments, with detectable signals at ~0.1 eV masses, especially at high redshifts (z~2).
AI.motivation: To characterize neutrino mass effects on cosmic web topology using advanced mathematical tools, addressing the long-standing challenge of neutrino mass detection in cosmology and particle physics.
AI.method: Apply discrete Morse theory, global topology, and persistent homology to analyze N-body simulations with massive neutrinos, focusing on filament statistics and persistence diagrams as scale-adaptive, parameter-free formalism.
AI.result: Neutrinos produce distinct, mass-dependent signatures on filaments and skeleton connectivity, most pronounced at high redshift (z~2) and detectable at few-percent level for masses as small as ~0.1 eV.
AI.conclusion: Filaments provide ideal environment for isolating neutrino effects; cosmic web topology and persistent homology offer promising avenue for constraining neutrino mass and hierarchy in upcoming galaxy surveys.

title: Beyond Mass and Multiscale Environments: What Shapes Low Surface Brightness Galaxies? Evidence from MaNGA
comment: 18 pages, 10 figures, accepted for publication in the Apj
summary: The origin of low surface brightness (LSB) galaxies remains a key open question in galaxy formation, reflecting the balance internal mechanisms and environmental influence. Using MaNGA integral-field spectroscopy, we investigate whether LSB and high surface brightness (HSB) galaxies of comparable stellar mass ($9 < \log M_\ast < 10$) occupy distinct environments or differ primarily through internal evolution. Our late-type sample comprises 113 central and 29 satellite LSB galaxies, and 374 central and 142 satellite HSB galaxies. We characterize environments on scales from 100 kpc to 10 Mpc, analyzing radial profiles of stellar mass surface density ($Σ_\ast$), star formation activity, and gas-phase metallicity. Central LSB and HSB galaxies inhabit similarly low-density large-scale ($>$200 kpc) environments, but LSB galaxies are more isolated on small scales ($\sim$100 kpc). Even after matching in stellar mass and environment, LSB galaxies show systematically lower $Σ_\ast$, $Σ_{SFR}$, and metallicities, often hosting diffuse, weakly star-forming bulges embedded in extended disks. These results indicate that LSB structure and star formation are not primarily governed by large-scale environment or halo mass. While secondary halo properties such as spin, concentration, or gas accretion history are often invoked, their environmental dependence appears weak. Instead, LSB-HSB differences for centrals likely reflect divergent assembly or interaction histories and internal processes -- such as angular momentum-driven disk evolution or inefficient gas conversion -- largely decoupled from large-scale environment. Nonetheless, environment still influences the observed star formation and chemical differences between central and satellite LSB galaxies.

AI.tldr: LSB galaxies differ from HSB galaxies primarily through internal evolution rather than large-scale environment, showing lower stellar density, star formation, and metallicity despite similar large-scale environments.
AI.motivation: To determine whether low surface brightness (LSB) galaxies form primarily due to environmental influences or internal evolutionary processes, addressing a key open question in galaxy formation.
AI.method: Used MaNGA integral-field spectroscopy to analyze 113 central and 29 satellite LSB galaxies compared to 374 central and 142 satellite HSB galaxies (stellar mass range 9 < log M* < 10). Characterized environments from 100 kpc to 10 Mpc scales, analyzing radial profiles of stellar mass surface density, star formation activity, and gas-phase metallicity.
AI.result: Central LSB and HSB galaxies inhabit similarly low-density large-scale (>200 kpc) environments, but LSB galaxies are more isolated on small scales (~100 kpc). Even after matching stellar mass and environment, LSB galaxies show systematically lower Σ*, ΣSFR, and metallicities, often hosting diffuse, weakly star-forming bulges in extended disks.
AI.conclusion: LSB structure and star formation are not primarily governed by large-scale environment or halo mass. Differences likely reflect divergent assembly/interaction histories and internal processes (angular momentum-driven disk evolution, inefficient gas conversion) largely decoupled from large-scale environment, though environment still influences central-satellite differences.

title: Analytic compression of the effective field theory of the Lyman-alpha forest
comment: 28 pages, 11 figures, 2 tables
summary: The 1D flux power spectrum ($P_{\mathrm{1D}}$) of the Ly$α$ forest provides an exceptionally high-resolution probe of structure formation down to small scales ($k\approx1-10~\text{$h~$Mpc$^{-1}$}$). These scales carry the imprints of massive neutrinos, warm dark matter, and the running of the primordial power spectrum spectral index. The effective field theory (EFT) is a promising perturbative approach to systematically and efficiently describe the Ly$α$ forest, but it faces challenges in its application to $P_{\mathrm{1D}}$, as many EFT parameters become degenerate when projected along the line of sight. In addition, this projection generates new stochastic terms from the integration over small-scale modes. In this work, we address these issues by compressing the EFT model space using the Fisher matrix formalism and linearizing the resulting compression directions, enabling analytic template marginalization and significantly reducing the computational cost of likelihood evaluation. We use hydrodynamical simulations to obtain a baseline estimate of EFT parameters, and use the DESI DR1 $P_{\mathrm{1D}}$ measurements to derive compression directions. We then marginalize over deviations from the baseline using these compression directions and forecast the constraining power of our formalism. We find that even in conservative scenarios where each data redshift bin requires its own set of EFT parameters, the cosmological constraints saturate with the linear bias, two leading-order 1D stochastic terms, and three principal combinations of the remaining EFT templates. In this case, our forecasted precision of the amplitude ($Δ^2_p$) and the logarithmic slope ($n_p$) of the linear matter power spectrum at the pivot scale ($k_p=0.7~\text{Mpc}^{-1}$) is $10\%$ and $2.0\%$, respectively, which is similar to emulator-based analyses that include observational data systematics.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a compressed EFT framework for analyzing 1D Lyα forest flux power spectra, using Fisher matrix compression and linearization to overcome parameter degeneracies and reduce computational costs, achieving cosmological constraints comparable to emulator-based methods.
AI.motivation: The 1D Lyα forest flux power spectrum provides high-resolution cosmological information on small scales, but applying effective field theory (EFT) to this observable faces challenges: parameter degeneracies from line-of-sight projection and generation of new stochastic terms from small-scale mode integration.
AI.method: Compress the EFT model space using Fisher matrix formalism, linearize the resulting compression directions to enable analytic template marginalization, use hydrodynamical simulations for baseline EFT parameter estimates, apply DESI DR1 measurements to derive compression directions, and marginalize over deviations from baseline using these directions.
AI.result: Cosmological constraints saturate with linear bias, two leading-order 1D stochastic terms, and three principal combinations of remaining EFT templates. Forecasted precision: 10% for amplitude (Δ²_p) and 2.0% for logarithmic slope (n_p) of linear matter power spectrum at pivot scale k_p=0.7 Mpc⁻¹, similar to emulator-based analyses with observational systematics.
AI.conclusion: The compressed EFT framework successfully addresses degeneracy and computational challenges in analyzing 1D Lyα forest power spectra, providing efficient cosmological constraints comparable to more computationally intensive methods while handling the complexities of line-of-sight projection.

title: Optical identification of the FASHI sources: toward the extended Local Volume
comment: Accepted for publication in Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: We extracted a list of 662 nearby (within $\sim16$ Mpc) HI-detection sources from the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) All Sky HI Survey (FASHI) and made a visual identification of them with optical counterpart. This inspection led to the discovery of 71 new dwarf galaxies. All of them are dwarf irregular galaxies with ongoing star formation. They are characterized by the following median parameters: visual magnitude of $g=17.8$ mag and color $(g-r)=0.29$ mag, HI-flux $S_\mathrm{HI}=718$ mJy km/s, HI-mass $M_\mathrm{HI}=3.7\times10^7$ $M_\odot$, as well as the HI line-width of $W_{50}=37$ km/s.

AI.tldr: Discovery of 71 new dwarf irregular galaxies from FAST HI survey data through optical counterpart identification
AI.motivation: To identify and characterize previously undetected dwarf galaxies in the nearby universe using HI survey data from the FAST telescope
AI.method: Extracted 662 nearby HI-detection sources from FAST All Sky HI Survey (FASHI) and performed visual identification with optical counterparts
AI.result: Discovered 71 new dwarf irregular galaxies with ongoing star formation, characterized by median parameters: g=17.8 mag, (g-r)=0.29 mag, HI-flux=718 mJy km/s, HI-mass=3.7×10⁷ M⊙, HI line-width=37 km/s
AI.conclusion: FAST HI survey enables discovery of previously undetected dwarf galaxies, expanding our census of low-mass galaxies in the local universe

title: Joining forces: 30 years optical monitoring of the Einstein Cross
comment: Accepted to A&A; 18 pages, 6 long tables (Tables C.1-C.6) are available at the CDS
summary: We present an extended optical monitoring of the quadruply-imaged gravitationally lensed quasar QSO 2237+0305, the Einstein Cross, including observations from different observatories in both hemispheres and using a new photometric technique. This technique uses a region far enough from the lens system to determine accurately the sky background level, and minimises contamination from the lensing galaxy by combining analytical and numerical modeling of its structure. The resulting light curves of the four quasar images describe variations across practically the entire optical spectrum and span about 9000 days in the $VRI$ bands. The multi-band microlensing variability is captured with an unprecedented level of detail, and a preliminary microlensing analysis reveals an almost linear scaling of source radius with wavelength, providing direct evidence for the wavelength-dependent structure of the region contributing to optical passband fluxes. Specifically, assuming a mean microlens mass $\langle M \rangle$ = 0.3 $\rm{M_{\odot}}$ and concentric Gaussian sources that move according to the velocity distribution peaks (speed and direction) reported in a previous microlensing analysis, we find that the half-light radius of the $g$-band source is 9.6 $\pm$ 2.7 lt-day and the size of the sources grows with wavelength with a power-law index of $α$ = 0.94 $\pm$ 0.05. We conclude that these long-term light curves set stringent empirical constraints on models of quasar emission and microlensing physics.

AI.tldr: Extended optical monitoring of gravitationally lensed quasar QSO 2237+0305 reveals wavelength-dependent source structure through detailed microlensing analysis, showing source size grows with wavelength with power-law index α = 0.94 ± 0.05.
AI.motivation: To obtain high-quality, long-term multi-band light curves of gravitationally lensed quasars to study microlensing variability and constrain the wavelength-dependent structure of quasar emission regions.
AI.method: Extended optical monitoring using multiple observatories with a novel photometric technique that accurately determines sky background and minimizes contamination from the lensing galaxy through combined analytical and numerical modeling.
AI.result: Generated 9000-day light curves in VRI bands capturing detailed microlensing variability; analysis reveals source radius scales linearly with wavelength (α = 0.94 ± 0.05), with g-band half-light radius of 9.6 ± 2.7 light-days.
AI.conclusion: The long-term light curves provide stringent empirical constraints on quasar emission models and microlensing physics, demonstrating wavelength-dependent structure of optical emission regions.

title: The k-MENDEL sample of local analogs to reionization galaxies. Spectral identification of EELGs and properties of green peas in DESI
comment: 21 pages (incl. appendix), 15 figures. Submitted to A&A
summary: Low-mass galaxies with intense starbursts exhibit spectra dominated by extreme nebular emission and faint stellar continua. These extreme emission-line galaxies (EELGs) are key laboratories to study star formation, feedback, and ionizing photon escape in low-metallicity environments. We exploit the DESI survey to assemble the k-Means of Extreme Nebulae from DEsi outLiers (k-MENDEL), a statistically robust sample of ~16,000 EELGs at 0.01 < z < 0.96 selected via automatic k-means classification. Using SED fitting and Te-based metallicities, we characterize EELGs including "blueberry" and "green pea" galaxies, spanning stellar masses of 10^6-10^10 Msun and SFRs of 0.1-100 Msun/yr. k-MENDEL extends previous SDSS samples toward higher redshifts and lower metallicities (12+log(O/H) ~ 7.0-8.5). EELGs lie systematically above the star-forming main sequence, with sSFRs up to ~100 Gyr^-1. They follow a shallower mass-metallicity relation offset by 0.3-0.5 dex from local relations, closely resembling young galaxies observed with JWST at z > 3-10. The large intrinsic metallicity scatter, even after projecting along the fundamental metallicity relation, indicates strong departures from simple "bathtub" models, suggesting massive inflows of metal-poor gas followed by strong feedback. While ~6% of the sample shows AGN-like signatures, the most extreme star-forming systems reach high ionization (O32 ~ 5-60) comparable to confirmed Lyman-continuum emitters. Our results support the interpretation of EELGs as short-lived, non-equilibrium phases in the evolution of low-mass galaxies and highlight their importance as nearby analogs of galaxies likely driving cosmic reionization (Abridged).

AI.tldr: DESI survey identifies ~16,000 extreme emission-line galaxies (EELGs) using k-means classification, revealing them as low-metallicity, high-sSFR systems that resemble high-redshift galaxies and may drive cosmic reionization.
AI.motivation: To study star formation, feedback, and ionizing photon escape in low-metallicity environments using extreme emission-line galaxies (EELGs) as laboratories, and to understand their role as nearby analogs of galaxies driving cosmic reionization.
AI.method: Used DESI survey data with automatic k-means classification to assemble k-MENDEL sample of ~16,000 EELGs at 0.01 < z < 0.96. Applied SED fitting and Te-based metallicities to characterize galaxy properties, including comparison with SDSS samples and JWST observations.
AI.result: EELGs have stellar masses 10^6-10^10 Msun, SFRs 0.1-100 Msun/yr, and metallicities 12+log(O/H) ~ 7.0-8.5. They lie above the star-forming main sequence with sSFRs up to ~100 Gyr^-1, follow a shallower mass-metallicity relation offset by 0.3-0.5 dex from local relations, and show large intrinsic metallicity scatter indicating non-equilibrium evolution.
AI.conclusion: EELGs represent short-lived, non-equilibrium phases in low-mass galaxy evolution, serving as nearby analogs of high-redshift galaxies that likely drove cosmic reionization, with their properties suggesting massive inflows of metal-poor gas followed by strong feedback.

title: The Cliff: A Metal-Poor Little Red Dot Hosting an Overmassive Black Hole at $z = 3.55$
comment: 20 pages, 17 figures. Submitted to MNRAS
summary: JWST has revealed a large population of massive black holes (BHs) in the early Universe with unusual properties which mark them as distinct from low-redshift active galactic nuclei. Such findings have prompted the development of new models of BH formation and growth, and of their co-evolution with host galaxies. Linking the gas-phase metallicity of BH environments to seed masses is key to understanding which evolutionary pathways could explain the population of JWST-discovered BHs. We present new high-resolution JWST NIRSpec/IFU observations covering the rest-frame optical emission lines of a Little Red Dot (LRD) at $z=3.55$, known as The Cliff, from the `Red Unknowns: Bright Infrared Extragalactic Survey' (RUBIES). We find evidence for low metallicity ($Z=0.017\pm0.004 \ Z_\odot$) based on the low narrow-line [OIII]$\lambda5007$/H$β$ ratio, supported by the non-detection of low-ionisation emission lines such as [OII]$λ\lambda3727,3729$ and [NII]$λ\lambda6548,6583$. We find that the observed properties of The Cliff, including its overmassive BH, can be reproduced by some simulations of black hole growth and evolution down to $z\sim3.5$. However, these simulation runs require high seed masses ($10^4 - 10^5\ M_\odot$) and appear as rarely in the simulation volume as in the RUBIES survey volume over redshifts $3<z<4$, highlighting the unusual nature of The Cliff. Future simulations and numerical models will help to uncover how such a metal poor system managed to develop a massive black hole and persist to such low redshift.

AI.tldr: JWST observations of a high-redshift Little Red Dot reveal low metallicity environment supporting massive black hole growth from high seed masses, challenging standard AGN evolutionary models.
AI.motivation: JWST has discovered unusual massive black holes in the early Universe with properties distinct from low-redshift AGN, requiring new models of BH formation and growth. Understanding the connection between gas-phase metallicity and BH seed masses is crucial for explaining these JWST-discovered systems.
AI.method: Used high-resolution JWST NIRSpec/IFU observations covering rest-frame optical emission lines of a Little Red Dot (LRD) at z=3.55 from the RUBIES survey. Analyzed narrow-line ratios ([OIII]λ5007/Hβ) and searched for low-ionization emission lines ([OII], [NII]) to determine metallicity.
AI.result: Found low metallicity (Z=0.017±0.004 Z⊙) based on low [OIII]/Hβ ratio and non-detection of low-ionization lines. The observed properties, including overmassive BH, can be reproduced by simulations requiring high seed masses (10⁴-10⁵ M⊙), but such systems are rare in both simulations and survey volume.
AI.conclusion: The Cliff represents an unusual metal-poor system that developed a massive black hole and persisted to low redshift. Future simulations and models are needed to explain how such systems form and evolve, challenging current understanding of BH-galaxy co-evolution in the early Universe.

title: An automated method for planetary nebula detection with SIGNALS: first applications to NGC 4214 and NGC 4449
comment: 21 pages, 19 figures, Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: Utilising the optical imaging Fourier transform spectrograph SITELLE, the Star-formation, Ionized Gas and Nebular Abundances Legacy Survey (SIGNALS) is designed to study the connection between star-forming regions and their environments. Targeting $31$ local star-forming galaxies, its data products also lend themselves to planetary nebula (PN) surveys. We present here a new pipeline to find PNe using automated emission-line diagnostics and morphology tests, that is able to distinguish PNe from contaminants with an accuracy similar to that of past visual methods. We also perform thorough completeness tests using mock PNe inserted into the data cubes with full spectra. We apply these tools to a pilot sample of two dwarf irregular galaxies from the SIGNALS survey, NGC 4214 and NGC 4449, with other galaxies to follow. For these two galaxies, we identify $25$ PNe (including $6$ new discoveries) and $23$ PNe (including $13$ new discoveries), respectively, and calculate PN luminosity function distances of $3.09^{+0.25}_{-0.46}$ and $3.91^{+0.33}_{-0.52}$ Mpc, respectively, the latter consistent with previous estimates. We also calculate the bolometric PN specific frequency of our galaxies ($α_\mathrm{bol}$), as well as a newly defined $V$-band PN specific frequency ($α_\mathrm{V}$) based solely on the galaxies' total luminosities in that band.

AI.tldr: A new pipeline for automated planetary nebula detection using SITELLE spectrograph data from SIGNALS survey, applied to two dwarf galaxies with distance measurements and PN specific frequencies.
AI.motivation: To develop an automated method for identifying planetary nebulae in SIGNALS survey data that matches the accuracy of visual methods while enabling systematic PN surveys across multiple galaxies.
AI.method: Created a pipeline using automated emission-line diagnostics and morphology tests to distinguish PNe from contaminants, with thorough completeness testing using mock PNe inserted into data cubes with full spectra.
AI.result: Applied to NGC 4214 and NGC 4449, identifying 25 PNe (6 new) and 23 PNe (13 new) respectively, with PN luminosity function distances of 3.09 Mpc and 3.91 Mpc, and calculated both bolometric and V-band PN specific frequencies.
AI.conclusion: The automated pipeline successfully identifies PNe with accuracy comparable to visual methods, enabling systematic PN surveys across the SIGNALS galaxy sample for distance measurements and stellar population studies.

title: Methanimine as a sink in the HCN and HNC solid state hydrogenation network
comment: Accepted in A&A (Apr 2026)
summary: We aim to provide a systematic and quantitative description of the hydrogenation network connecting HCN and HNC to methylamine on interstellar water ices, while identifying dominant pathways and bottlenecks. To this end, we performed a comprehensive quantum-chemical investigation of H-addition, H-abstraction, reactions with H2, and water-assisted H-transfer isomerization, covering intermediates linking HCN and HNC to CH3NH2. Calculations were carried out on amorphous solid water clusters of 14 molecules. Using benchmarked density functional theory, we derived activation barriers, elucidated mechanisms, and determined the binding energy distribution of H2CN and CNH2, also assessing deuterium substitution effects. H-addition reactions generally involve activation barriers, except for radical species. Considering both barrier heights and tunneling crossover temperatures, the most favorable sequence originates from HNC rather than HCN. The network evolves toward methanimine (H2CNH), the central species, or the singlet carbene HC:NH2, from which further hydrogenation leads to methylamine. Along these paths, several reactions are barrierless, while some H-abstraction processes compete with addition. Reactions involving H2 are uncommon, as most are endoergic. Deuterium substitution weakly affects classical barriers but significantly influences tunneling efficiencies. Our results support efficient formation of methanimine and methylamine from HNC on cold interstellar ices, with methanimine acting as a chemical sink, whereas HCN is less reactive and more likely to persist. These findings provide quantitative constraints for astrochemical models.

AI.tldr: Systematic quantum-chemical study of hydrogenation pathways from HCN/HNC to methylamine on interstellar water ices reveals HNC as preferred starting point, with methanimine as key intermediate and chemical sink.
AI.motivation: To provide quantitative understanding of hydrogenation networks connecting HCN and HNC to methylamine on interstellar water ices, identifying dominant pathways and bottlenecks for astrochemical modeling.
AI.method: Comprehensive quantum-chemical investigation using benchmarked DFT on amorphous solid water clusters (14 molecules), analyzing H-addition, H-abstraction, H2 reactions, and water-assisted H-transfer isomerization mechanisms.
AI.result: HNC is more reactive starting point than HCN; methanimine (H2CNH) serves as central intermediate/chemical sink; several barrierless reactions exist; H2 reactions are uncommon; deuterium substitution affects tunneling efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Efficient methylamine formation occurs from HNC on cold interstellar ices via methanimine intermediate, providing quantitative constraints for astrochemical models of prebiotic molecule formation.

title: Constraining the Molecular Kennicutt-Schmidt Relation with Multi-Transition CO Observations of Nearby Galaxies
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ, 5 figures, 13 pages
summary: The relationship between the star formation rate surface density and the molecular gas surface density in galaxies is key to understanding galaxy evolution. To investigate the molecular Kennicutt-Schmidt (K-S) relation and its dependence on gas density, we analyze a uniform sample of 36 nearby galaxies from the AMISS survey, focusing on the CO(1-0), CO(2-1), and CO(3-2) transitions, which trace progressively denser and warmer molecular gas. Using statistical methods that combine binning with Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) fitting, we derive the slope, scatter, and intercept of the $Σ_{\mathrm{SFR}}$-$Σ_{\mathrm{CO}}$ relation for each transition. We find power-law slopes of 1.26, 1.14, and 1.07 for CO(1-0), CO(2-1), and CO(3-2), respectively, consistent with a trend toward increasingly linear star formation relations at higher-J transitions. This behavior supports the idea that denser gas is more directly linked to ongoing star formation and is consistent with previous findings of near-linear correlations between HCN or high-J CO luminosities and global SFR. The observed trend suggests an underlying relation between gas and SFR volume densities with a power-law index of $\sim$1.5, indicating enhanced star formation efficiency in denser environments. These findings underscore the critical role of dense gas in regulating star formation and highlight the importance of tracer selection and excitation conditions when interpreting the K-S relation across different environments.

AI.tldr: Analysis of molecular Kennicutt-Schmidt relation across CO transitions shows increasingly linear star formation relations for higher-J transitions, indicating denser gas is more directly linked to ongoing star formation.
AI.motivation: To investigate the molecular Kennicutt-Schmidt relation and its dependence on gas density by analyzing how different CO transitions (tracing progressively denser/warmer gas) relate to star formation rate surface density.
AI.method: Analyzed uniform sample of 36 nearby galaxies from AMISS survey focusing on CO(1-0), CO(2-1), and CO(3-2) transitions. Used statistical methods combining binning with Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) fitting to derive slope, scatter, and intercept of Σ_SFR-Σ_CO relation for each transition.
AI.result: Found power-law slopes of 1.26, 1.14, and 1.07 for CO(1-0), CO(2-1), and CO(3-2) respectively, showing trend toward increasingly linear relations at higher-J transitions. This supports denser gas being more directly linked to star formation. Trend suggests underlying relation between gas and SFR volume densities with power-law index ~1.5.
AI.conclusion: Denser gas plays critical role in regulating star formation. Tracer selection and excitation conditions are important when interpreting Kennicutt-Schmidt relation across different environments. Higher-J CO transitions show more linear correlation with star formation, indicating enhanced star formation efficiency in denser environments.

title: Paschen Jumps in Little Red Dots: Evidence for Nebular Continua
comment: 7 pages, 6 figures, submitted to A&A. Comments are welcome
summary: ''Little Red Dots'' (LRDs) are broad-line sources at high redshift, initially identified by their compact morphologies, red colours and prominent Balmer breaks. The origin of their optical-to-near-infrared continua is debated, with proposed explanations ranging from direct recombination emission to thermalised blackbodies from stellar-like atmospheres. Here we report evidence for Paschen jumps in a subset of LRDs, consistent with free-bound recombination to hydrogen $n=3$. The Paschen and Brackett continuum shapes across the sample are consistent with minimally reddened emission from low-temperature gas with $T_e\lesssim10\,000$ K, while the presence of Paschen jump signatures limits scenarios in which the emission is thermalised. Further, the extreme H$α$ equivalent widths and the tight observed correlation between H$α$ and the continuum follow naturally if both originate in recombination emission. This provides an observational upper limit on the contribution of any direct AGN accretion component and any stellar-atmosphere-like component, as well as on the fraction of line emission that can be thermalised as it traverses the cocoon. Ultimately, nebular radiative-transfer models provide a self-consistent explanation of the continuum, line strengths and line profiles without requiring multiple separately fitted components.

AI.tldr: LRDs show Paschen jumps indicating free-bound hydrogen recombination, constraining emission mechanisms and limiting AGN/stellar contributions.
AI.motivation: To determine the origin of optical-to-NIR continua in Little Red Dots (LRDs) and resolve the debate between recombination emission vs. thermalized blackbody scenarios.
AI.method: Analysis of Paschen and Brackett continuum shapes across LRD sample, examination of Paschen jump signatures, correlation between Hα and continuum, and nebular radiative-transfer modeling.
AI.result: Paschen jumps consistent with free-bound recombination to hydrogen n=3; continuum shapes indicate minimally reddened emission from low-temperature gas (Te ≲ 10,000 K); extreme Hα equivalent widths and tight Hα-continuum correlation support recombination origin; limits contributions from AGN accretion and stellar-atmosphere components.
AI.conclusion: Nebular radiative-transfer models provide self-consistent explanation of continuum, line strengths, and profiles without requiring multiple components, favoring recombination emission over thermalized scenarios.

title: The missing ultra-faint satellites of the Milky Way
comment: 19 pages, 15 figures. Submitted to MNRAS
summary: We combine the highest resolution N-body simulation of a $\sim 10^{12}\, M_\odot$ $Λ$CDM halo (Aquarius-A) with the {\sc GALFORM} galaxy formation semianalytic model to study the full satellite population expected in a MW-like galaxy. The model assumes that galaxies only form in subhalos whose peak circular velocity exceeds the H-cooling threshold, all of which are well resolved in the simulation. The number of luminous subhalos ever accreted into the main halo is thus well defined, and implies that the total number of MW satellites, down to arbitrarily low luminosity, should not exceed a few hundred. The model tracks satellites even after their halos cease to be resolved ("orphan" galaxies), and includes a novel treatment of dark matter and stellar tidal stripping which takes into account that all $Λ$CDM subhalos survive until the present because of their cuspy inner density profiles. After accounting for tides, our results match well the massive end of the observed MW satellite mass function and predict that a large number of ultra-faint dwarfs are missing from the current MW satellite census. The missing UFDs are predicted to avoid the innermost regions of the host, and to have properties that overlap with those of the many ultra-faint compact MW satellites (UFCSs) discovered recently, with properties intermediate between globular clusters and dwarf galaxies. Our results suggest that many UFCS systems are dark matter-dominated dwarfs with velocity dispersions between $1-3$km/s, which have survived disruption because they reside in the dense cusp of $Λ$CDM subhalos. UFCSs should have mean densities of order $10^{10}$-$10^{11}\,M_\odot/$kpc$^3$, higher than those of more extended ultra-faint systems. If confirmed, our results would provide support for the cuspy nature of $Λ$CDM dark matter halos and for the hydrogen-cooling threshold for galaxy formation.

AI.tldr: Combining high-resolution N-body simulation of a Milky Way-like halo with GALFORM galaxy formation model to study satellite population, predicting missing ultra-faint dwarfs that avoid inner regions and have properties intermediate between globular clusters and dwarf galaxies.
AI.motivation: To understand the full satellite population in Milky Way-like galaxies, reconcile predictions from ΛCDM cosmology with observations, and address the "missing satellites" problem by studying ultra-faint dwarf galaxies.
AI.method: Combines highest-resolution N-body simulation of a ∼10¹² M⊙ ΛCDM halo (Aquarius-A) with GALFORM semianalytic galaxy formation model. Includes novel treatment of dark matter and stellar tidal stripping, tracks "orphan" galaxies after their halos cease to be resolved, and assumes galaxy formation only in subhalos exceeding H-cooling threshold.
AI.result: Predicts total Milky Way satellites should not exceed a few hundred down to arbitrarily low luminosity. Matches massive end of observed MW satellite mass function after accounting for tides. Predicts many missing ultra-faint dwarfs that avoid innermost regions, with properties overlapping ultra-faint compact satellites (UFCSs) - intermediate between globular clusters and dwarf galaxies. UFCSs should be dark matter-dominated with velocity dispersions 1-3 km/s and mean densities 10¹⁰-10¹¹ M⊙/kpc³.
AI.conclusion: Results support cuspy nature of ΛCDM dark matter halos and hydrogen-cooling threshold for galaxy formation. Many ultra-faint compact systems are likely dark matter-dominated dwarfs that survived disruption due to residing in dense cusps of ΛCDM subhalos.
